Kelvin works out the order one pad at a time, and the worst case is that every wrong guess is tried before the right one.

**Cost of wrong guesses.** Suppose Kelvin already knows the first k−1 pads. To test a candidate for the k-th pad, he re-hops the k−1 known pads and then hops to the candidate, which is k hops per failed attempt. Position k has 10−k+1 candidates, so in the worst case he fails 10−k times before only one remains. That remaining pad is identified by elimination, with no wrong hop needed.

The wrong-guess cost over all positions is

Σ_{k=1}^{9} k(10−k) = 10·45 − 285 = 165.

**Final successful run.** Once the full order is known, he hops on all 10 pads and then to the other side, which is 11 hops.

**Total:** 165 + 11 = 176.

ANSWER: 176
